newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Rollovers seen aiding efficient SAfrica govt spend.
newsitem.headline: Rollovers seen aiding efficient SAfrica govt spend.

text.p: Rollovers, which saved the state 14 billion rand ($3.2 billion) between 1992/93 and 1996/97, had proved an effective way of ensuring state funds were spent efficiently, director general of state expenditure Hannes Smit said.

"Obviously, we would not have saved all that, and...there would have been quite a sum in there that would have been wasted, without that system," he told the parliamentary finance committee on Friday.
Rollovers had initially been introduced in 1992/93 to prevent government departments from wasting unspent funds before the end of each financial year as the money could not be kept.
"Although the reason for rollovers has changed over time, we think that it is a good instrument to ensure the efficient spending of government funds," Smit said.
Controls on rollovers had been tightened since last year and Smit said that he believed that they should be maintained.
In 1992/93, a 1.4 billion rand rollover was approved, but 4.1 billion rand was surrendered at the end of the year. In 1993/94, 3.4 billion rand was allowed and 8.4 billion rand was surrendered.
In 1995/96, rollovers totalled 6.8 billion rand and 13 billion rand was surrendered, of which 8.9 billion was rolled over into 1996/97.

Smit said the increase in rollovers since 1994, despite the greater social needs of South Africa's first non-racial government, was due to new departments taking longer than expected to reprioritise spending and plan and implement projects.
